examples.solution_text:
(a) The index $3$ means three factors of $6$.
$\begin{aligned}6^{3}&=6\times6\times6\\&=36\times6\\&=216\end{aligned}$
(b) Multiply the three equal factors.
$\begin{aligned}7\times7\times7&=49\times7\\&=343\end{aligned}$

(a) An index of $1$ means one factor.
$73^{1}=73$
(b) Multiplying twenty-four factors of $1$ still gives $1$.
$1^{24}=1$
(c) Multiplying six factors of $0$ gives $0$.
$0^{6}=0$

examples.question_text:
(a) Evaluate $10^{6}$ as a basic numeral.
(b) Write $100\,000\,000$ as a power of $10$.
examples.solution_text:
(a) $10^{6}$ means six factors of $10$.
$\begin{aligned}10^{6}&=10\times10\times10\times10\times10\times10\\&=1\,000\,000\end{aligned}$
(b) $100\,000\,000$ is a $1$ followed by eight zeros.
$100\,000\,000=10^{8}$

examples.question_text:
(a) Write $5040$ in expanded form using powers of $10$.
(b) Write $2\times10^{4}+6\times10^{2}+9$ as a basic numeral.
examples.solution_text:
(a) Split the number by place value. The hundreds and ones digits are zero.
$\begin{aligned}5040&=5000+40\\&=5\times10^{3}+4\times10^{1}\end{aligned}$
(b) Evaluate each power, then add the place-value amounts.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}2\times10^{4}+6\times10^{2}+9\\&=20\,000+600+9\\&=20\,609\end{aligned}$

Evaluate both powers before comparing.
$2^{7}=2\times2\times2\times2\times2\times2\times2=128$
$7^{2}=7\times7=49$
Since $128>49$, $2^{7}$ is larger.

(a) Two negative factors give a positive product.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}(-6)^{2}\\&=(-6)\times(-6)\\&=36\end{aligned}$
(b) Three negative factors give a negative product.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}(-6)^{3}\\&=(-6)\times(-6)\times(-6)\\&=36\times(-6)\\&=-216\end{aligned}$

The index $3$ means three factors of $0.4$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}(0.4)^{3}\\&=0.4\times0.4\times0.4\\&=0.16\times0.4\\&=0.064\end{aligned}$
